_readme: THE PUBLISHABLE-INPUTS ALLOWLIST — [pipeline 9]R-12 Private/requirements/ (was pipeline/09-release-engineering.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15)
Every value any workflow compiles INTO a Flutter artifact, with the reason it is safe to ship and
the residual risk of shipping it. A `--dart-define` is not a secret store: the value is written
into the AOT snapshot or the JS bundle, so on web it is one `view-source` away and on every other
platform it is one `strings` away. 'It came from `secrets.`' says where the value was KEPT, never
where it ENDS UP.
WHY AN ALLOWLIST AND NOT A SCANNER. A scanner for 'things that look like secrets' cannot be
written: SUPABASE_ANON_KEY is a JWT and is designed to ship; GLITCHTIP_DSN contains what reads
like a password and is designed to ship; E2E_PASSWORD is a real password and must NEVER reach a
published artifact. The three are indistinguishable by shape. What CAN be checked is that a human
wrote down, once, why each one is here — and that the written-down set and the shipped set are
THE SAME SET.
🔴 SET EQUALITY, BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE POINT.
· a define no entry covers        -> FAIL. Nobody ships a value without stating what it costs.
· an entry no workflow passes     -> FAIL. Otherwise a name can be PRE-APPROVED — approved
today, added months later by somebody who reads the entry as permission and never re-asks the
question. It is also how a dead entry survives the removal of the thing it justified.
`reason` answers 'why may this be read by anyone who downloads the app'. `residual` answers 'and
what does it still cost us that it can be'. An entry with a reason and no residual is the shape
that gets waved through, so the guard requires both and refuses a blank one.
⚠️ THIS IS NOT tooling/capability-register.json's QUESTION. That register classifies E2E_EMAIL /
E2E_PASSWORD for VENDOR review — 'which third party sees this'. This file asks 'does this end up
in bytes a stranger downloads'. Same two names, two different questions, two different answers.

_why: The workflows scanned for `--dart-define` and `--dart-define-from-file`. Derived from the
directory rather than listed, so a NEW workflow acquires the obligation by existing. The guard
folds `run: >` blocks before matching — a line-based scan finds a fraction of the real surface,
and ci.yml documents that exact trap in its own comment beside assert-vendor-portability.

SUPABASE_URL.reason: The project URL is the address of a public API endpoint. Every browser request to Supabase carries it in the clear, so it is public the moment the app makes its first call — compiling it in changes nothing about who can see it.
SUPABASE_URL.residual: It names our project to anyone reading the bundle, which is a target for credential-stuffing and for enumeration of the anon-key surface. The protection is Row Level Security on the tables, not obscurity of the host.

SUPABASE_ANON_KEY.reason: Supabase's anon key is DESIGNED to ship in clients — it is the browser-side identity every Supabase web app publishes. It grants exactly what Row Level Security lets it grant and nothing more.
SUPABASE_ANON_KEY.residual: It is a working key for unauthenticated access, so every RLS policy is the ONLY thing between it and the data. A table shipped with RLS off is fully readable by anyone who reads the bundle, and the key cannot be rotated without a release.

API_BASE_URL.reason: The hostname of our own Worker, which the app contacts on every launch. It is in DNS and in every request; a client cannot call an address it does not know.
API_BASE_URL.residual: It hands an attacker the endpoint list to probe without having to install the app first. Mitigated by the Worker's own auth and CORS allowlist, never by hiding the host.

APP_VERSION.reason: The build's own version string. It IS the artifact's identity — it is what analytics rows, consent artifacts and crash reports are attributed to, and a version nobody can read is a build nobody can attribute.
APP_VERSION.residual: It discloses the exact build a user is running, which narrows a search for known defects in that build. Accepted: the alternative is untraceable production data.

GLITCHTIP_DSN.reason: A Sentry/GlitchTip DSN is a WRITE-ONLY ingest key and is designed to ship inside every client — that is how a crash reporter reports. It cannot read an issue, a project or an event.
GLITCHTIP_DSN.residual: Anyone who reads it out of the bundle can POST events into our project: spam, noise, and quota burn on a self-hosted instance with finite storage. The remedy is rate limiting and rotation, not concealment.

TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY.reason: 🔴 THE ONE ENTRY WHOSE VALUE IS SUPPOSED TO BE READ OUT OF THE BUNDLE. A Cloudflare Turnstile SITE key is the public half of a keypair and it only works when it is in the page: the browser hands it to Cloudflare's widget script to fetch a challenge. The half that decides anything is the SECRET key, which lives on the auth box as CAPTCHA_SECRET, never reaches this repository and is what /siteverify checks. Passed from a repository VARIABLE rather than a secret precisely so that nothing here pretends it is one.
TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY.residual: It names our Turnstile widget to anyone reading the bundle, so a scripted client can mint challenges against our widget and burn its quota, and the widget's domain allowlist (subly.nikatru.com + localhost) is what stops a token minted elsewhere being useful. Rotating it is a REDEPLOY, not a config edit (tooling/capability-register.json records that as this vendor's exception), and it stops being cheap at the first store release, when installed clients would hold the old key until they update. APPENDED 2026-09-07: while the repository variable is unset the define reaches the WEB deploy empty and TurnstileGate renders nothing at all — deploy-web.yml ships that state deliberately, so the cutover window carries no workflow edit for this channel. e2e.yml no longer accepts it: its preflight fails CLOSED on an empty sitekey, because a live suite that signs in with no captcha token proves the suite passes WITHOUT the gate and says nothing about the stack it exists to rehearse (scope 7.4.9 - a green run with an empty sitekey is not acceptance). The key reaches ONE of the thirteen shipping build steps; the twelve store and desktop lanes carry the identity defines and not this one, which is a residue recorded in phase3-cutover-blockers.md 8.6 (residue R10; this pointer said 8.2 until 2026-09-07 - 8.2 is the empty-sitekey section) and becomes a live defect at the first store release. ⏱ APPENDED 2026-09-09, AND THE APPENDED-2026-09-07 SENTENCE ABOVE IS NOW FALSE — it is left standing because the sequence is the record. THE VARIABLE IS SET AND THE GATE IS LIVE: `gh variable list` returns TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY = 0x4AAAAAAEmJbm3bI8bk4wno, set 2026-09-07T06:09:24Z, and that literal is COMPILED INTO THE DEPLOYED BUNDLE — found today inside the TurnstileGate constructor in https://nikatru.com/subly/main.dart.js. So this row's `residual` is no longer a description of a future state. 🔴 AND THE DOMAIN ALLOWLIST NAMED IN THIS ROW — `subly.nikatru.com + localhost` — IS THEREFORE A LIVE DEFECT, NOT A STALE NOTE. [ADR 075] moved the app's published address to https://nikatru.com/<id>; a Turnstile widget validates the hostname the challenge is requested from against that list, so on the address the app is now actually served at the challenge is refused, and the four gated auth screens with it. The allowlist was written when the app owned a whole origin and nothing re-read it when the origin moved — the same class as an expiry date nobody re-reads. 👤 IT IS NOT REPAIRABLE FROM THIS REPOSITORY AND NO EDIT HERE SHOULD PRETEND OTHERWISE: the SITE KEY is a --dart-define this repo passes, but the widget's DOMAIN LIST is a Cloudflare Turnstile console setting with no in-tree representation. Owner step, recorded in full at docs/ci/deploy-web.md: Turnstile → the widget for this site key → Settings → Domains → ADD nikatru.com, KEEP subly.nikatru.com (it is still the 301 source and the apex router's proxy origin, so removing it breaks arrivals through legacy links) and KEEP localhost. One domain added, none removed, no key rotation, no redeploy. ⏱ APPENDED 2026-09-15 — THE "TWELVE STORE AND DESKTOP LANES CARRY ... NOT THIS ONE ... BECOMES A LIVE DEFECT AT THE FIRST STORE RELEASE" SENTENCE ABOVE IS SUPERSEDED BY [ADR 084] (owner, 2026-09-15, "Store builds skip it"). The absence is now the DESIGN: Turnstile guards web sign-in only, the key is read once in apps/subscriptiontracker/lib/core/app_config.dart (AppConfig.turnstileSiteKey / isTurnstileConfigured), and tooling/ci/assert-store-build-config.mjs grades it both ways — every web lane MUST pass it (W1), every store lane MUST NOT (W2). So installed store clients never hold this key, and the "stops being cheap at the first store release" clause no longer applies. Revisit trigger, from the ADR: bot sign-ups observed on a native channel.

REVENUECAT_KEY.reason: RevenueCat's PUBLIC SDK key (goog_... on Play, appl_... on Apple) is DESIGNED to ship inside the app: the purchases SDK sends it on every call to identify the project, exactly as RevenueCat's own docs tell every client to. It can fetch offerings and post receipts for validation by the stores; it cannot read customers, grant entitlements or change products. The key that can is the SECRET v2 key, which lives only in the vault and never reaches a --dart-define. One define, fed per store rail from REVENUECAT_PUBLIC_KEY_GOOGLE or REVENUECAT_PUBLIC_KEY_APPLE, as channel-register.json's storeKeyDefine records.
REVENUECAT_KEY.residual: Anyone who reads it out of the bundle can call RevenueCat as our app: fetch our offerings and prices (already public in the store) and post receipts, which the stores themselves validate, so a forged receipt grants nothing. The cost is request noise against our project. It cannot be rotated without a release.

E2E_AUTH_TARGET.reason: 🔴 NOT A PUBLISHED VALUE, AND NOT A CREDENTIAL EITHER. The literal string `hosted` or `boxa`, naming which auth stack the live E2E run was pointed at. It reaches only e2e.yml's `flutter drive` build — a DEBUG web build served to a headless Chrome on the runner and destroyed with the runner — and it selects which of two POSITIVE expectations the suite asserts: hosted answers a wrong password with the invalid-credentials copy, Box A refuses it at the captcha first. In the same class as APP_ENV: it names a branch, not a key.
E2E_AUTH_TARGET.residual: It tells a reader of the run's logs which auth stack a given E2E run graded, which is the whole point of it — a run whose name says `boxa` and whose suite silently graded production is the false green this axis exists to make impossible. Nothing about it is sensitive; it is recorded here because set equality is checked in both directions and a define with no entry is refused.

APP_ENV.reason: The literal string `production`. It selects which config branch the app takes and is not a credential in any sense.
APP_ENV.residual: None beyond confirming the build is the production one, which the version already says.

RELEASE_CHANNEL.reason: The id of the channel this artifact was built for — a row id in tooling/channel-register.json, e.g. `web`. It is a fact ABOUT the binary, in the same class as the version string, and a user can read it off their own copy of the app with no consequence.
RELEASE_CHANNEL.residual: It tells a reader which distribution channel a given binary came from, which narrows a search for channel-specific defects in that build. Accepted for the same reason as APP_VERSION: the alternative is artifacts that cannot be told apart.

E2E_EMAIL.reason: 🔴 NOT A PUBLISHED VALUE. It reaches only `e2e.yml`'s `flutter drive` build — a DEBUG web build served to a headless Chrome on the runner and destroyed with the runner. Nothing that carries it is uploaded, deployed or published. The account itself is created by tooling/e2e/provision_user.mjs at the start of the run and purged by tooling/e2e/purge.mjs at the end.
E2E_EMAIL.residual: If the purge ever fails, the account outlives the run. The address is throwaway and carries no data, but a stale account accumulates in the auth table where nobody is looking for it.

E2E_PASSWORD.reason: 🔴 THE ENTRY THAT MATTERS MOST, AND ITS REASON IS ENTIRELY ABOUT SCOPE. This is a real password for a real Supabase account, and it is acceptable ONLY because it is generated per run for a throwaway user, is passed to a build that is never published, and is purged at `e2e.yml`'s teardown. There is no reading under which this value may be compiled into a shipped artifact.
E2E_PASSWORD.residual: If the purge ever fails — a cancelled run, a runner killed mid-job, a Supabase outage during teardown — a live account's password sits in the build logs and the process table of a public repository's workflow. It is scoped to one throwaway user with no data, but it is a working credential and it does not expire on its own. Writing that down is most of this entry's value: the day somebody reuses this define on a lane that publishes, the reason above is what makes the mistake obvious.

E2E_TOKEN_HASH.reason: A SINGLE-USE magic-link token for one throwaway E2E user, minted per run by tooling/e2e/provision_user.mjs via admin/generate_link and exchanged once at /verify. It exists because Box A enforces Turnstile on token?grant_type=password, so a headless driver cannot log in by typing credentials at all after the cutover. Acceptable on the same terms as E2E_PASSWORD and on one stronger term: it is passed to a build that is never published, it belongs to a throwaway user purged at teardown, AND it is spent by the first exchange - a replay returns HTTP 403, measured against Box A 2026-09-04.
E2E_TOKEN_HASH.residual: Strictly SMALLER than E2E_PASSWORD's, and the difference is the point. A leaked password is a standing credential that does not expire on its own; this token dies the moment the run uses it, which it does within seconds. The window where a leaked value is live is the gap between provisioning and the driver's first sign-in. What it does NOT reduce is the blast radius if the purge fails, because the USER still exists - that residual belongs to E2E_EMAIL and E2E_PASSWORD and is unchanged here.

E2E_DELETE_EMAIL.reason: 🔴 NOT A PUBLISHED VALUE, and it is a SECOND throwaway address rather than a reuse of E2E_EMAIL for a reason that is not cosmetic: golden-path leg 6 (`account delete purges`) makes the app really delete the account it signs in with, and the first user's row is what `tooling/e2e/verify_row.mjs` asserts still exists after the drive. Same scope as E2E_EMAIL in every other respect — created by tooling/e2e/provision_user.mjs at the start of the run, reaches only e2e.yml's `flutter drive` debug build served to a headless Chrome on the runner, and nothing that carries it is uploaded, deployed or published.
E2E_DELETE_EMAIL.residual: Identical to E2E_EMAIL's, with one difference in the happy case: this account is normally destroyed by the app itself mid-run, so the window in which it exists is shorter. On a run that fails before the delete walk it is a stale account like any other, and tooling/e2e/purge.mjs is what removes it.

E2E_DELETE_PASSWORD.reason: 🔴 A REAL PASSWORD FOR A REAL SUPABASE ACCOUNT, on exactly the terms E2E_PASSWORD is accepted on and no wider: generated per run for a throwaway user, passed to a build that is never published, and purged at e2e.yml's teardown. It is passed twice inside the app — once to sign in, once to RE-AUTHENTICATE at the delete-account dialog, which refuses to enable its destructive button until a password has been typed. There is no reading under which this value may be compiled into a shipped artifact.
E2E_DELETE_PASSWORD.residual: Same as E2E_PASSWORD's: if the teardown ever fails, a working credential for a live account sits in the build logs of a public repository's workflow, and it does not expire on its own. It is scoped to one throwaway user whose only data is the single subscription the run itself created.

E2E_DELETE_TOKEN_HASH.reason: The same, for the second throwaway user the delete-account leg drives. Separate define because the token is single use: one exchange per user, and the two legs sign in independently.
E2E_DELETE_TOKEN_HASH.residual: Identical to E2E_TOKEN_HASH's. Recorded separately rather than cross-referenced because a shared note is a note that gets edited for one entry and read for two.
